instruction: We act for Braport Seed Genetics, Inc. in its supply arrangement with Traidir Seed Production, LLC. Braport is the customer here and owns the proprietary parent-line germplasm that Traidir will work with, so we need a clear view of where the documents leave Braport exposed before the client relies on them for the 2027 production season. Please review the full matter folder: supply_agreement.md, statement_of_work_2027.md, service_level_schedule.md, and production_planning_meeting_notes.md. Prepare a memo to me that lists each issue you identify, says where it appears (document and section), explains why it matters for Braport, and gives a recommended fix. Where a fix calls for drafting changes, include proposed language if you can. If any point turns on facts we would need from the client, flag it as an open question rather than assuming. Keep the memo practical and organized so I can use it to brief the client and decide what to raise with Traidir. Let me know if anything in the folder looks incomplete or missing.

rubric.text: The response identifies that the exclusivity and non-production covenant in Supply Agreement Section 4.1, read with the Section 1.1 definitions of "Contract Seed" (any seed of any crop from Braport Germplasm) and "Territory" (United States and Canada), extends beyond the hybrid corn, Iowa-and-Illinois scope recorded in SOW Section 1.1. It locates the issue in Supply Agreement Section 4.1 and/or Section 1.1, explains why this matters to Braport, and recommends a fix.
hints: hybrid corn in Iowa and Illinois

rubric.text: The response identifies that Supply Agreement Section 18.2 lets Traidir assign the Agreement without Braport's consent, including to a competitor that would then hold Braport's parent seed. It locates the issue in Supply Agreement Section 18.2, explains why this matters to Braport, and recommends a fix.

The response identifies that Service Level Schedule Section 6.2 subjects Germplasm Loss Events to the Supply Agreement Section 12.2 fee cap, overriding the Section 12.3(a) carve-out for Article 9 germplasm breaches, and that the Schedule prevails under Supply Agreement Section 2.3. It locates the issue in Service Level Schedule Section 6.2, explains why this matters to Braport, and recommends a fix.

The response identifies that Service Level Schedule Section 8.1 sends seed-quality, performance failure and service credit disputes to Iowa law and the Polk County, Iowa courts, and that because the Schedule prevails under Supply Agreement Section 2.3, this overrides the Delaware law and Wilmington forum in Sections 19.1 and 19.2. It locates the issue in Service Level Schedule Section 8.1, explains why this matters to Braport, and recommends a fix.
The response states that the Supply Agreement order of precedence (Section 2.3) ranks the Service Level Schedule first, then the Supply Agreement, then each Statement of Work.
The response states that the Supply Agreement Section 12.2 liability cap equals the fees paid by the customer in the 12 months preceding the claim.
The response is organized as a memo addressed to the supervising partner, and for each issue it presents the location (document and section), why it matters, and a recommended fix.
The response claims that the narrower hybrid-corn, Iowa-and-Illinois scope in the Statement of Work controls over the Supply Agreement exclusivity definitions under the order of precedence.
The response claims that the Supply Agreement's Delaware governing law and Wilmington forum clauses prevail over the Iowa law and forum provision in Service Level Schedule Section 8.1.
